subject: Discovery recap: HealthLytics LLM sourcing & migration criteria
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: HealthLytics LLM sourcing & migration criteria

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our conversation so we have a shared checklist and clear next steps. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Call summary (high level)
- Primary goal: remove dependency on proprietary API contracts and move to an open/model-agnostic inference stack with predictable cost and hosting options (hosted + dedicated).
- Primary drivers: cost predictability, data residency controls (PHI-adjacent), lower vendor lock-in, and better tail-latency for live triage use cases.

Pain points you called out
- Heavy monthly spend on GPT-4/Anthropic for real-time scoring and chat flows (spikes cause throttling).
- Lack of first-party control for session affinity / KV cache — rebuilding state across calls is costly.
- Embeddings parity and drift: upstream vector storage relies on exact tokenization and embedding shapes.
- Procurement and security are risk-averse: need SOC2 evidence, clear data handling, and residency options.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Model APIs: OpenAI GPT-4 Turbo (primary) + Anthropic Claude for some assistants.
- Frontend: web+mobile chat, synchronous scoring endpoints, ephemeral session storage in Redis.
- Vector DB: Pinecone for semantic search with 1536-d embeddings.
- Monthly usage estimate: ~2.5B tokens (combined) with 400–600 req/sec peaks.

Success criteria for a migration proof point
- Match functional parity: streaming, function-calling / tooling, deterministic embeddings (or mapped parity), and session caching capability.
- Latency: p95 tail latency under 300ms for scoring paths in dedicated capacity mode.
- Cost: demonstrable 40–60% unit-cost improvement or comparable with better latency predictability.
- Security: SOC2+ data residency in US-East / US-West, option for dedicated private deployment.

Model shortlist (initial thinking)
- Llama 2 / Meta variants (65B) — strong accuracy, needs infra for latency-sensitive paths.
- Mistral / Mistral-Instruct-style (7–8B) — cost-efficient for many assistant tasks.
- Red7B quantized (example internal variant) — candidate for dedicated fast-paths and caching.

Immediate next steps
1) Send compatibility checklist (attached) — please fill sections on embeddings & tokenization quirks.
2) Schedule technical deep-dive (Rishi + infra) next week — link below.
3) Procurement: we’ll follow up with a ballpark pricing matrix + SOW draft after the technical call.

Attachments: redwood-compatibility-checklist.xlsx, redwood-prelim-estimate.pdf

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Johnson <alex@healthlytics.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@healthlytics.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 12:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: HealthLytics LLM sourcing & migration criteria

Lauren — thanks for the thorough summary, this matches my notes. A few clarifications / asks from our side:

- Volume: the 2.5B token figure is the current aggregated consumption; for the migration pilot we expect to route ~5% of traffic (~125M tokens / month) to validate latency and embeddings parity.
- Priority: latency for patient-facing triage is the highest priority; scoring paths (batch jobs) can tolerate higher latency.
- Embeddings: we need either exact parity with our current 1536-d vectors or a clear migration mapping with reindexing guidance.

Procurement is looped in on this thread — Laura in procurement will want an initial ballpark for a pilot (monthly committed vs burst) and a list of compliance artifacts (SOC2 report, encryption at rest details, and data residency options).

Can Rishi or Ben join the technical deep-dive? We prefer Wed (May 6) or Thu (May 7) morning PT.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering
HealthLytics
alex@healthlytics.com | (212) 555-9987

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: HealthLytics LLM sourcing & migration criteria

Alex / team — great, thanks for the extra color. We can do Wed May 6 at 9:00am PT for an infra-focused deep-dive. Ben will cover runtime & batching; Rishi will bring the model/compatibility checklist.

Quick answers and what we’ll bring to the call:
- Pilot sizing: recommend a pilot with a small dedicated pool sized for 125–200M tokens/month (we’ll provide a tiered estimate in the SOW). See redwood-prelim-estimate.pdf attached.
- Embeddings parity: typical migration options are (1) reproduce the same embedding model (if available) or (2) re-embed with a recommended model + reindex. For Pinecone we’ve migrated customers with a reindex window and backfill script; we’ll include a migration script template in the repo.
- Session affinity / KV cache: we’ll demo our KV cache patterns and how we can persist and restore model-side caches to avoid rewarm penalty. This is a common ask and something we can replicate in the pilot.

Model shortlist notes (brief)
- Llama 2 family: good accuracy; expect higher infra cost for 65B if you need low tail-latency.
- Mistral / smaller instruct-tuned models: strong cost/quality tradeoff for assistant flows.
- Quantized 7B variants: best for dedicated fast-paths with aggressive batching + cache.

Compatibility checklist items we’ll want completed before the deep-dive: tokenization samples for top 10 prompts, a sample embedding from your pipeline, peak qps patterns, and a short list of tool-calls we need to preserve (websearch, internal KB).

Links: technical deep-dive calendly: https://calendly.com/redwood/healthlytics-technical-deep-dive
Evaluation repo (read-only): https://drive.redwood.com/healthlytics/eval-repo

Attachments: healthlytics-llm-shortlist.csv (simple model/cost matrix)

Next steps summary
1) Team fills and returns the compatibility checklist (Alex / engineering).
2) Deep-dive Wed May 6 9:00am PT — Ben + Rishi attend.
3) Post-deep-dive: draft SOW + pilot pricing + SOC2 evidence pack for Procurement.

Talk soon — I’ll send calendar invite.

—
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com
